title: Model lock negotiation: pin precedence, fallback and SDK surface
creator: Avery Chen
description: Clarify and implement a deterministic negotiation and enforcement strategy for model version pins across the public API and SDKs. The goal is to allow callers to pin by tag (e.g., 'stable', 'redwood-recommended'), semver ranges (e.g., '^2.3.0'), and immutable identifiers (commit hash / artifact id), and to define precise precedence, fallback behavior, runtime compatibility checks, and observable audit records. This ticket covers API semantics, SDK ergonomics, runtime resolver contract, and rollout plan for changing default precedence rules.
background: Customers require predictable behavior when they request specific model versions. Current code paths mix tag-resolution, semver heuristics, latest-tag fallback, and runtime affinity heuristics which have led to surprising rollouts. We must provide a single, documented pin negotiation algorithm that the SDKs adopt and the runtime enforces, plus clear error messages and telemetry when mismatches occur.
proposed_design: 1) API/SDK pin grammar: accept three pin types - tag (string), semver selector (string), immutable_ref (hex or artifact id). 2) Precedence order (highest->lowest): immutable_ref > exact_semver > semver_range > explicit_tag > implicit_default. 3) Runtime compatibility: when a resolved candidate is incompatible with requested profile (quantization, architecture), runtime attempts safe fallbacks in precedence order; if none succeed, return an explicit 409-like ContractMismatch error with recommended alternatives and a resolver_trace in telemetry. 4) SDK behavior: expose Pin object with methods .byTag(), .bySemver(), .byRef(); provide a Pin.ResolveOptions to control strictness (strict | best_effort | allow_fallback). 5) Audit: every resolution request logs resolver_trace (ordered steps) and final_resolved_ref. 6) Migration: keep old default behavior for two cycles behind a feature flag, then flip the new precedence with a console-visible changelog.
acceptance_criteria: API accepts Pin payloads with explicit pin_type field and validation errors for malformed semver/ref
SDK exposes Pin builders and ResolveOptions; default is 'best_effort' with telemetry opt-in
Runtime implements deterministic resolver using precedence and produces resolver_trace in logs
When a pin cannot be satisfied due to compatibility, runtime returns ContractMismatch with suggested candidates
Upgrade path exists behind feature flag and documented in changelog and migration guide
Unit + integration tests cover tag->semver->ref resolution and fallback scenarios
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): land SDK and API changes behind feature flag; enable for internal Redwood services and 2 pilot customers. Phase 2 (beta): enable for early adopters, add console opt-in and clearer UI for pinned models. Phase 3 (general): flip default precedence flag, publish migration guide, and increase telemetry retention for resolver_traces for two weeks. Fall back plan: revert feature flag and start directed incident runbook if >1% error rate or significant customer regressions.
risks_mitigation: Risk: existing clients that relied on implicit older precedence may observe different models. Mitigation: feature flag, 2-cycle opt-in, clear migration doc, and a 'compatibility mode' setting in SDK to preserve legacy behavior. Risk: perf regression from extra resolution calls. Mitigation: cache resolved artifact ids per model/tag and add TTL, add sampling for resolver_trace.
test_plan: Unit tests for parser/validator for semver and refs; e2e tests against the resolver with mocked model catalog including incompatible candidates; chaos tests to validate graceful fallbacks under network partial failure; telemetry assertions for resolver_trace presence and structure.
open_questions: Should semver comparisons support build metadata and pre-release identifiers for default precedence?
What is the canonical immutable_ref format (git sha vs artifact uuid)?
Do we allow mixing pins in a single request (e.g., user supplies both semver and tag)? If so, which wins?
What retention period for resolver_trace logs is acceptable for privacy/compliance?
implementation_notes: SDK changes should be backwards-compatible: new Pin object compiles down to existing model selector fields. REST API introduces optional 'pin_type' and 'pin_value' top-level fields; existing requests without pins default to runtime policy. Runtime resolver adds metrics: pin_resolution_latency_ms, pin_resolution_failures, and a structured resolver_trace string.
